Flash flood at Manshiya district, water about 1.5m, a family stuck on 2nd floor, elderly person struggling to breathe.
Need drinking water and baby formula at Agami shelter school, about 120 people, since yesterday.
Road blocked by fallen electricity pole on Corniche near Stanley bridge. Live wire in water. Nobody hurt yet.
BREAKING!!! dam collapsed in Alexandria, thousands dead, share now!!!
Clinic in Sidi Gaber lost power, 6 dialysis patients waiting, generator fuel ends in 3 hours.

stages.verification:
Merged Incident 1 (R1 + R2)  
Need: rescue  
Location: Manshiya district  
Life‑threatening: true  
Summary: A flood in Manshiya district has trapped a family on the second floor, with an elderly person having difficulty breathing.  
Verification: VERIFIED – corroborated by two independent reports (Arabic and English) describing the same situation.

Merged Incident 2 (R3)  
Need: water_food

People affected: 120

Location: Corniche near Stanley Bridge

Summary: A fallen electricity pole has blocked the road on the Corniche near Stanley Bridge, with a live wire in the water.

stages.triage:
P1 – Incident 1: Verified flood trapping a family; elderly person struggling to breathe requires immediate rescue.  
P1 – Incident 3: Fallen electricity pole with live wire in water creates instant electrocution danger to anyone nearby.  
P2 – Incident 5: Six dialysis patients at Sidi Gaber clinic will lose power in ~3 hours, threatening lives if fuel isn’t restored.  
P3 – Incident 2: 120 people at Agami shelter need water and baby formula; urgent but not immediately life‑threatening.  
P3 – Incident 4: Rumored dam collapse with no verification; no confirmed casualties, thus lowest priority.
stages.dispatch:
1. Incident 1 – Resource: Swift‑water rescue unit with EMT/paramedic.  
   First safe action: Secure a stable entry point, deploy a rescue boat or rope system, and evacuate the breathing‑distressed elder to shore for immediate medical care.  
   Hazard to check: Flood‑water current strength and potential building collapse or hidden debris.

2. Incident 3 – Resource: Electrical‑hazard response team with insulated rescue gear and de‑energizing equipment.  
   First safe action: Isolate the live wire (turn off upstream breaker or use insulated cutters) before any personnel enter the water.  
   Hazard to check: Presence of standing water conducting electricity and possible secondary pole collapse.

3. Incident 5 – Resource: Mobile generator crew with fuel supply and biomedical support staff.  
   First safe action: Position the generator at a safe distance, connect it to the clinic’s power system, and begin continuous monitoring of dialysis machines.  
   Hazard to check: Fuel spill/flammability risk and generator exhaust ventilation.

4. Incident 2 – Resource: Water‑distribution team with tanker trucks, bottled water, and infant‑formula kits.  
   First safe action: Set up a safe distribution point away from shelter entrances, verify water quality, and begin immediate hand‑out to the 120 occupants.  
   Hazard to check: Contaminated water sources and crowd‑control safety (trip hazards, slip risk).

5. Incident 4 – Resource: Reconnaissance team with UAV/ground survey assets.  
   First safe action: Conduct remote visual inspection of the dam to confirm structural status before any ground deployment.  
   Hazard to check: Unstable dam embankment or sudden release of water if collapse is imminent.

Urgent: Live wire in water at Corniche near Stanley Bridge. Isolate power, keep distance, avoid water entry until secured.
